articles.title: Nucleic acid therapeutics for reinvigorating p53 function in glioblastoma: concepts, limitations and recent advances.
articles.abstract: IDH-wildtype, high-grade glioma with predominantly astrocytic differentiation and classified as glioblastoma in the current WHO classification of central nervous system tumors is among the most common and aggressive primary malignant brain tumors. Glioblastoma remains largely refractory to current therapies, leading to early recurrence and poor prognosis. In nearly all glioblastomas, the p53 tumor-suppressor pathway is functionally inactivated, either through TP53 mutations or through deregulated signaling pathways that promote p53 degradation. This review provides a comprehensive and up-to-date overview of gene therapy strategies designed to restore p53 function or exploit p53 loss-of-function in glioblastoma. In particular, it critically discusses the biological barriers and technical limitations of viral and non-viral nucleic acid delivery systems that have contributed to inadequate clinical outcomes, while also highlighting recent advances with potential to reinvigorate p53 function in glioblastoma.

articles.title: Navigating the landscape of stem cell therapeutics: Overcoming translational hurdles via emerging technologies and regulatory frontiers.
articles.abstract: Global population aging has increased the incidence of intractable diseases. Accordingly, regenerative medicine using stem cell therapies offers a critical shift from symptom management to functional tissue restoration. Hematopoietic, mesenchymal, and pluripotent stem cells (embryonic and induced pluripotent stem cells) have shown promising therapeutic potential. However, their clinical translation is constrained by persistent biological, manufacturing, and regulatory hurdles associated with genomic instability, tumorigenic risk, and batch-to-batch heterogeneity. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the current stem cell research landscape, highlighting the strategic shift from traditional cell-centric development to a multi-disciplinary and technology-driven approach. Emerging technologies, including three-dimensional organoids, advanced biomaterials, genome editing, and artificial intelligence-integrated automated manufacturing, are actively resolving long-standing translational bottlenecks to ensure scalable, safe, and reproducible clinical implementation. Regulatory approaches differ across major countries; however, the trend toward incorporating patient needs is growing. This has accelerated access to innovative therapies, with ongoing efforts to ensure that these advances do not compromise safety or efficacy. Moving forward, the successful clinical integration of next-generation stem cell therapeutics is likely to be shaped by the synergy between harmonized regulatory requirements and reliable real-world evidence. Collectively, these factors serve to bridge the transition from early patient access to definitive licensing.

articles.title: Neural programs of therapy resistance in cancer: A mechanism-first framework for therapeutic targeting.
articles.abstract: Neural regulation of cancer therapy resistance is established unevenly across tumor types, signal sources, and treatments. This review proposes an evidence-calibrated framework that evaluates each candidate mechanism through its source, signal or activity pattern, receptor, target cell, and treatment context. We organize candidate neural contributions into four author-defined, overlapping analytical programs: survival and damage tolerance; cell-state plasticity and drug-tolerant persistence; neuroimmune suppression; and metabolic, vascular, and stromal adaptation. These categories facilitate comparison rather than denote equally established mechanisms: survival and selected neuroimmune routes have more direct treatment-linked support than many vascular and stromal hypotheses. Local innervation is distinguished from systemic neuroendocrine signaling and non-neuronal ligand production, while circuit integration in brain tumors is separated from predominantly paracrine and perineural interactions in peripheral cancers. An explicit hierarchy differentiates prospective biomarker-supported clinical benefit (Level 1), early interventional pharmacodynamic evidence (Level 2), treatment-specific preclinical intervention evidence (Level 3), and association (Level 4). Source resolution and rescue are assessed separately within each study. Therapy-associated sprouting, receptor adaptation, and cancer-induced nerve injury are evaluated as distinct processes; current evidence does not establish treatment-induced neural rewiring as a universal resistance driver. Study-level comparisons, model-selection criteria, and operational biomarker examples identify where neural targeting is supported, where only pathway-level dependence is demonstrated, and where additional causal validation is required. The framework is intended to improve selection and interpretation of mechanism-matched combinations, rather than infer oncologic efficacy from the availability of neuromodulatory drugs.

articles.title: Benzo[a]pyrene vs. Tapinarof: unraveling ligand-specific AHR transcriptional responses in immortalized keratinocytes.
articles.abstract: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) integrates structurally diverse ligands to control xenobiotic metabolism, immune responses, and cell fate decisions. Ligand-specific AHR effects in human skin are increasingly recognized, but underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we compared transcriptomic responses of immortalized human keratinocytes to the environmental AHR ligand benzo[a]pyrene (BaP) and the therapeutic AHR agonist Tapinarof. Using AHR-proficient and AHR-mutant HaCaT keratinocytes, we performed bulk RNA-sequencing, pathway enrichment analysis, and targeted validation by qPCR and immunoblot analyses. Both ligands elicited largely AHR-dependent yet distinct gene expression programs. As expected, both ligands increased the expression of canonical AHR/ARNT pathway target genes, including cytochrome P450 (CYP) 1A1, CYP1B1, and artemin. However, BaP uniquely activated a non-canonical AHR signaling pathway involving epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and downstream signaling that stimulates NRF2 transcriptional activity. Tapinarof, while initiating similar initial events (e.g., c-Src phosphorylation), interfered with this pathway by inhibiting phosphoinositide 3-kinase/AKT signaling. Another gene set related to antiviral responses was also solely modulated by BaP and sensitive to CYP1A inhibition. This gene set also responded to etoposide, which induces DNA double-strand breaks independently of AHR. Indeed, inhibiting CYP1A-catalyzed metabolic activation of BaP reduced the level of phosphorylated histone H2AX, a marker for DNA double-strand breaks, and respective gene expression. Collectively, our data show that BaP and Tapinarof engage overlapping but mechanistically distinct AHR-dependent networks in immortalized keratinocytes, with BaP uniquely combining non-canonical AHR-EGFR-NRF2 signaling and CYP1A1-dependent genotoxic stress responses. Our results further suggest an off-target effect of Tapinarof, i.e., AKT inhibition.

articles.title: Gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase-responsive lipid PtIV prodrug amphiphile with tumor-selective uptake for enhanced chemotherapy.
articles.abstract: The limited tumor selectivity of cisplatin contributes to off-target exposure and dose-limiting toxicity. Here, we developed an enzyme-activatable, axially functionalized PtIV prodrug amphiphile for γ-glutamyl transpeptidase (GGT)-responsive cellular uptake and intracellular activation. The amphiphilic prodrug, consisting of a hydrophobic hexadecyl alkyl chain and a γ-glutamyl-functionalized peptide headgroup, spontaneously self-assembled into colloidally stable nanoparticles (GPtIV). GGT-mediated cleavage of the γ-glutamyl group shifted the surface charge of GPtIV from negative to positive and enhanced cellular uptake in GGT-high tumor cells. Pharmacological inhibition of GGT attenuated GPtIV uptake in 4T1 cells, further supporting the contribution of GGT activity to cellular internalization. Following cellular uptake, GPtIV underwent reductive activation under reducing conditions and released cisplatin. GPtIV exhibited enhanced cytotoxicity toward GGT-high tumor cells and preferential tumor accumulation in 4T1 tumor-bearing mice. At the tested Pt dose, GPtIV achieved greater tumor growth inhibition and improved renal and hepatic tolerability relative to the comparator Pt formulations. These findings support GGT-responsive charge conversion as a strategy for improving the cellular delivery and therapeutic performance of self-assembling PtIV prodrugs in GGT-high tumors.

articles.title: Triple-modal visualized radiohydrogel alleviates post-embolization hypoxia via stage-type procedure in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Transarterial radioembolization (TARE) holds significant potential for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but its effectiveness is hindered by radiation resistance from the post-embolization hypoxic microenvironment and challenges in achieving stable local release of radionuclides. Herein, polydopamine (PDA)-coated MnO2 nanoparticles (MnO2@PDA) with a core-shell structure were introduced as the intratumoral hydrogen peroxide nanocatalyst, and 177Lu was anchored in catechol groups on the PDA surface, achieving the stability of radionuclides. And the radionuclide-coordinated nanocatalyst was incorporated into the poly(ethylene oxide) and poly(propylene oxide) thermosensitive hydrogel to formulate an integrated TARE agent (177Lu-MnO2@PDA-Gel), facilitating secondary encapsulation and ensuring intratumoral retention of radionuclides without leakage. Through a three-stage lytic process, 177Lu-MnO2@PDA-Gel produced oxygen by gradually consuming endogenous H2O2. This allowed for post-embolization radiosensitivity and anti-angiogenesis. Furthermore, the release of manganese ions from the embolic hydrogel can serve as an adjuvant to boost intratumoral immune infiltration and improve the efficacy of embolization and internal radiation. Notably, the superiority of SPECT/PAI/MRI triple-modal imaging via 177Lu-MnO2@PDA-Gel enables real-time and dynamic visualization of TARE. Overall, the smart hydrogel demonstrates long-term oxygen generation, stable internal radiation, and tumor microenvironment remodeling, offering a sequential radiosensitization strategy to address TARE refractoriness, thereby presenting significant clinical value for locoregional therapy of HCC.

articles.title: Immunosuppressive termination of pro-inflammatory miRNA degradation via circular RNA nanosponge for sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy treatment.
articles.abstract: Managing inflammatory cytokine storms is prevalent in treatment of sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SICM), yet it remains a challenge to immunosuppression weaning. We herein propose an immunosuppressive termination of pro-inflammatory microRNA-33 (miR-33) degradation strategy for on-demand anti-inflammatory management. Inspired by circular RNA (cRNA) sponging capacity, we designed a miR-33-targeted sequence of cRNA (cRNA-33), including 11 of miR-33 binding sites and a single microRNA-223 (miR-223)-specific immunosuppression binding site. To improve drugability, cRNA-33 is compressed into reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive polymeric assembly, and covered by tannic acid-modified hyaluronic acid to enhance cardiac inflammatory macrophage accumulation. Triggered by intracellular ROS, cRNA-33 rapidly dissociates from assembly and binds sufficient miR-33 to alleviate inflammatory actions of NLRP3 and IL-1β induction. Macrophages are subsequently shifted from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory phenotype, resulting in high expression of miR-223 that destabilizes cRNA-33 through the miR-223-responsive site to discontinue immune responses. The cRNA-33 treatment yields 80% decrease of inflammation efficacy, 90% cardiac function recovery and 87.5% survival rate in study mice. Collectively, this study has provided an advanced anti-inflammatory therapy for SICM, at a safe level.

articles.title: Ionizable lipid impact on mRNA vaccine formulation properties and immunogenicity.
articles.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted global supply chains, causing shortages of critical lipid-based raw materials for mRNA vaccine production. To enhance formulation resilience, we systematically evaluated the impact of five ionizable lipids (ILs) on lipid nanoparticle (LNP) organization, mRNA delivery and immunogenicity. The physiochemical analysis revealed the potential coexistence of liquid crystalline lamellar (Lα) and inverse hexagonal (HII) phases, or a mixture of nucleotide-loaded and non-loaded HII phases within developed LNP formulations. Furthermore, ILs with saturated, multi-tail structures, such as Lipid-5 and SM-102, favored inverse hexagonal (HII) internal organization and fusion intermediates, correlating with enhanced endosomal fusion and higher in vivo protein expression. In contrast, ILs such as cKK-E12, which featured dual ionization headgroups and tended to form lamellar-like structures, showed reduced encapsulation efficiency and transfection potency. The preclinical experiments demonstrated that all developed formulations induced robust binding and neutralizing antibody responses; however, antibody responses were lower in mRNA Lipid 5 LNPs and mRNA SM-102 LNPs than in other formulations. Notably, within the limited panel of ILs in this study, protein expression levels did not show a clear correlation with antibody titers, highlighting that efficient antigen expression alone is not predictive of humoral immunity. These findings underscore how IL structural features influence LNP architecture and function, informing the rational design of next-generation mRNA vaccines.

articles.title: Sustained degradation of glucose transporter 1 by an mRNA-encoded lysosome-targeting chimera triggers metabolic collapse and pyroptosis in cancer.
articles.abstract: Cancer cells are intrinsically addicted to glucose and require glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)-mediated glucose metabolism for their survival. Although small-molecule inhibitors of GLUT1 have exhibited suppressive effects on tumor cells, they achieve only transient functional blockade, thereby limiting therapeutic durability and permitting metabolic escape. Here, we report MetaTAC-G1, an mRNA-encoded lysosome-targeting chimera that enables rapid and sustained degradation of cell-surface GLUT1. MetaTAC-G1 comprises a bispecific binder that bridges GLUT1 to the lysosomal trafficking receptor sortilin, thereby directing constitutive lysosomal clearance of the transporter upon translation. For local intratumoral delivery, we encapsulated the MetaTAC-G1-encoding mRNA in RGD-functionalized lipid nanoparticles (RGD-LNPs), achieving efficient mRNA expression and sustained GLUT1 degradation. Functionally, MetaTAC-G1 induced profound metabolic collapse in SUM159PT cells, characterized by acute ATP depletion and reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, culminating in GSDMD-dependent pyroptosis. Similar pyroptosis-associated morphological changes were observed across multiple additional cancer cell lines. In vivo, a single treatment course of MetaTAC-G1 markedly suppressed tumor growth and produced durable antitumor activity without apparent systemic toxicity. Our findings highlight that sustained degradation of GLUT1, rather than transient functional inhibition, is critical for triggering metabolic cell death in tumors.

articles.title: Reprogramming tumor-associated macrophages via ID3 mRNA delivery for enhanced immunotherapy in pancreatic cancer.
articles.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) features a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment dominated by tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), which facilitate immune evasion and compromise immunotherapeutic efficacy. The interaction between signal regulatory protein α (SIRPα) on macrophages and cluster of differentiation 47 (CD47) on tumor cells delivers a "don't-eat-me" signal that inhibits the phagocytosis of tumor cells by macrophages. Here, we present a macrophage-directed mRNA delivery strategy to reprogram TAMs in PDAC. Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) were engineered to deliver inhibitor of DNA binding 3 (ID3) mRNA, whose expression was associated with reduced SIRPα expression and pro-inflammatory macrophage reprogramming. To promote preferential uptake by TAMs, mannose-modified LNPs (MLNPs) were developed by exploiting elevated CD206 expression on these cells. In an orthotopic PDAC model, MLNP-mediated ID3 mRNA delivery enhanced macrophage phagocytosis, promoted pro-inflammatory immune remodeling, and increased intratumoral T cell and natural killer cell (NK) infiltration, accompanied by tumor-growth suppression. Furthermore, MLNP-ID3 showed enhanced combination activity with anti-PD-1 therapy. Collectively, these findings establish a macrophage-targeted mRNA strategy for transcriptional reprogramming of TAMs and present a promising immunotherapeutic framework for PDAC.

articles.title: A trifluoromethylated chalcone derivative attenuates Alzheimer disease-related Aβ/Tau pathology by modulating the AMPK-dependent autophagy-proteostasis axis.
articles.abstract: Impaired autophagic clearance contributes to proteostasis failure and the accumulation of amyloid-β (Aβ) and pathological Tau in Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet pharmacologically tractable activators of productive autophagy remain limited. Here, we screened an in-house library of 64 natural products, semisynthetic derivatives, and synthetic analogues and identified compound 51 (C51), a synthetic trifluoromethylated 4-hydroxy-3-methoxy chalcone derivative, as an activator of autophagy. C51 enhanced autophagic flux, lysosomal activity, and SQSTM1/p62 turnover in mammalian cells and Caenorhabditis elegans, indicating productive autophagic clearance rather than autophagosome accumulation. C51 reduced APP-, Tau-, and TauP301L-associated proteotoxicity in neuronal cells and ameliorated Aβ- and Tau-related behavioral deficits, protein aggregation, Tau phosphorylation, and oxidative stress in transgenic C. elegans. In 3×Tg-AD mice, C51 improved learning and memory, preserved hippocampal neurons and synaptic proteins, and reduced gliosis, Aβ oligomer accumulation, and phosphorylated Tau burden without overt systemic toxicity. Mechanistically, C51 activated AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and suppressed mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations, together with drug affinity-responsive target stability and cellular thermal shift assays, supported C51-AMPK interaction. AMPK knockdown, Compound C, and aak-2 RNA interference markedly attenuated C51-induced autophagy and protection against Aβ/Tau toxicity, demonstrating a conserved requirement for AMPK signaling. Quantitative proteomics further showed that C51 rebalanced TauP301L-disrupted proteostasis networks. Collectively, C51 represents a potent natural product-inspired autophagy activator with therapeutic potential for AD by restoring AMPK-dependent autophagic clearance and Aβ/Tau proteostasis across complementary AD models.

articles.title: Caffeine attenuates Aβ-induced hippocampal dysfunction alongside changes in adenosine receptor-linked GABA handling and neuronal excitability.
articles.abstract: Synaptic and circuit dysfunction in the hippocampus is an early feature of Alzheimer's disease, involving disturbances at both excitatory and inhibitory synapses. Adenosine receptors (ARs) regulate hippocampal glutamatergic and GABAergic signaling. Caffeine, a non-selective AR antagonist, has well-established neuroprotective actions. We examined whether caffeine attenuates amyloid-β (Aβ)-induced changes in neuronal viability, GABA handling, intrinsic excitability and synaptic excitation/inhibition (E/I) balance, and whether these functional effects occur alongside changes in AR and GABA transporter 1 (GAT-1) protein abundance. Primary mouse hippocampal cultures were exposed to Aβ1-42 (1nM) and/or caffeine (0.1, 1, 25, and 50µM) for culture-based assays, whereas acute hippocampal slices were exposed to Aβ1-42 (100nM) and/or caffeine (25µM) during whole-cell patch-clamp recordings from CA1 pyramidal neurons. In cultures, Aβ increased neuronal death, confirming previous reports, and caffeine co-treatment attenuated this effect. Total GAT-1, A1R and A2AR protein levels were unchanged, whereas Aβ reduced neuronal A1R immunoreactivity; this reduction was not observed with caffeine co-treatment. Radiometric assays identified treatment-associated differences in 1-h 3H-GABA accumulation and basal 3H-GABA outflow, including a non-significant trend toward increased accumulation after Aβ exposure and reduced accumulation in the Aβ+caffeine condition. In slices, Aβ flattened the frequency-current relationship and transiently reduced the E/I ratio, whereas these changes were not observed during caffeine co-application; subsequent caffeine exposure restored firing output after 30min of Aβ exposure. Further experiments are required to establish if changes in A1R immunoreactivity or radiometric GABA handling contribute to the electrophysiological effects.

articles.title: Gut Dubosiella newyorkensis alleviates noise-related atherosclerosis by reducing N1-methyl-4-pyridone-3-carboxamide.
articles.abstract: Environmental noise is ubiquitous in daily life and has emerged as a major risk factor for cardiovascular diseases. Nevertheless, the association between noise exposure and coronary heart disease, as well as the underlying molecular mechanisms, remains poorly understood. Here, analyses of UK Biobank (UKB) data revealed that noise exposure was associated with an increased risk of coronary heart disease. We further demonstrated that noise exposure elevated circulating levels of N1-methyl-4-pyridone-3-carboxamide (4PY) in both humans and rodents. Accumulation of 4PY suppressed endothelial NR4A1 expression, activated NF-κB signaling, facilitated monocyte adhesion and inflammatory cytokine release, and ultimately accelerated atherosclerotic progression. Mechanistically, we found that noise exposure reduced the abundance of Dubosiella newyorkensis (D. newyorkensis) in the gut microbiota of humans. Supplementation with D. newyorkensis upregulated hepatic ACMSD expression, lowered circulating 4PY levels, and alleviated noise-related atherosclerotic progression in mice. Our findings provide mechanistic insights into the therapeutic potential of D. newyorkensis in mitigating noise-related atherosclerosis by reducing circulating 4PY levels. Targeted modulation of the gut microbiota may represent a promising strategy for preventing and managing cardiovascular complications triggered by environmental noise.

articles.title: Repurposed catechol-O-methyltransferase inhibitors tolcapone and entacapone preferentially suppress aggregation and seeding of P301 mutant tau in human neuronal models.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Pathogenic aggregation and propagation of seed-competent TAU assemblies drive tauopathies. MAPT P301 mutations accelerate aggregation and enhance seed competence, yet pharmacological strategies selectively targeting these pathogenic species remain limited. We investigated whether the clinically approved catechol-O-methyltransferase inhibitors tolcapone (TOL) and entacapone (ENT) preferentially modulate mutant TAU aggregation and seeding. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: TOL and ENT effects on TAU aggregation were evaluated via cell-free assays, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), and in silico docking. Functional consequences of compound-modified fibrils were assessed in mutant TAU-expressing SH-SY5Y cells. Translational relevance was examined in human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived neurons exposed to pathogenic K18 fibrils, followed by post-seeding compound treatment. KEY RESULTS: Both compounds dose-dependently inhibited TAU aggregation, exhibiting greater potency, stronger SPR binding affinities, and more favourable computed interaction energies for P301S mutant versus wild-type TAU. Fibrils formed with TOL or ENT induced less downstream TAU oligomerization and phosphorylation in SH-SY5Y cells, with TOL showing superior protection. In hiPSC-derived neurons, post-seeding treatment with either compound decreased fibril-induced, sarkosyl-insoluble, TAU aggregation and phosphorylation without overt cytotoxicity. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: TOL and ENT preferentially reduced the aggregation and seeding of pathogenic P301 mutant TAU in the experimental models examined. These findings provide proof-of-concept support for mutation-focused pharmacological approaches and identify catechol scaffolds as starting points for developing more potent and safer TAU-directed compounds. Further studies are required to define the relevant molecular interactions, confirm the neuronal findings across additional hiPSC lines and determine whether effective CNS exposure can be achieved in vivo.

articles.title: Pigeonpea leaves in orthopedic diseases: bioactive metabolites, pharmacological actions and therapeutic potential.
articles.abstract: Pigeonpea leaves are derived from Cajanus cajan (L.) Huth [Fabaceae] and have long been used in traditional medicine to relieve blood stasis, swelling, pain, and musculoskeletal disorders. Flavonoids, stilbenes, phenolic acids, and triterpenoids are among the main metabolite classes identified in pigeonpea leaves. Experimental studies have linked pigeonpea leaf-derived materials to changes in inflammatory and oxidative-stress-related outcomes, microcirculation, and bone metabolism. Accordingly, their potential relevance to orthopedic disorders, including osteonecrosis of the femoral head, osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, and bone defects, has attracted increasing interest. Reported preclinical effects include changes in osteogenic differentiation, osteoclast formation, local blood supply, lipid metabolism, and inflammation- or oxidative-stress-related tissue injury. Among the investigated materials, total-flavonoid fractions, stilbene-rich extracts, the purified metabolite cajanin, and Tongluo Shenggu Capsule have shown biological activity in experimental models. This review summarizes the current research on pigeonpea leaves and their extracts, fractions, purified metabolites, and preparations in orthopedic disorders and discusses their possible mechanisms of action, potential relevance to orthopedic disorders, limitations of the available evidence, and remaining research gaps.

articles.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of targeted systemic therapies for prurigo nodularis: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Prurigo nodularis (PN) is a chronic, intensely pruritic inflammatory skin disease. Multiple targeted biologic therapies have shown efficacy against placebo, but no randomized trial has directly compared these agents, leaving their relative efficacy and safety uncertain. To compare the efficacy and safety of dupilumab, nemolizumab, vixarelimab, and serlopitant for PN using network meta-analysis. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched for randomized trials enrolling adults with PN that evaluated dupilumab, nemolizumab, vixarelimab, or serlopitant against placebo or one another. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2. A frequentist network meta-analysis was performed, with treatment effects expressed as risk ratios (RR) or standardized mean differences (SMD) with 95% CIs and surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) values. Certainty of evidence was assessed using CINeMA. Eight randomized trials (1652 participants; mean age, 53.5 years) were included. At week 4, vixarelimab, 540 mg, produced the largest reduction in itch severity (SMD, - 2.36; 95% CI, - 3.28 to - 1.44), a finding sustained at week 16 (SMD, - 1.26; 95% CI, - 1.96 to - 0.55). Nemolizumab, 60 mg, produced the highest rate of clinically meaningful itch response (≥ 4-point PP-NRS improvement) at week 4 (RR, 6.77; 95% CI, 2.85-16.13) and was the only treatment with a sustained response advantage at weeks 12 to 16 (RR, 3.37; 95% CI, 1.45-7.84). For Investigator's Global Assessment success, nemolizumab, 30 mg, ranked highest (RR, 4.24; 95% CI, 2.46-7.29). No active treatment was associated with a significant increase in overall adverse events, serious adverse events, or infections; however, dupilumab was associated with more treatment discontinuations (RR, 13.01; 95% CI, 4.12-41.06) and serlopitant with more nasopharyngitis (RR, 5.41; 95% CI, 1.25-23.45). Certainty of evidence was low for most outcomes. Vixarelimab and nemolizumab ranked highest for itch severity and clinically meaningful itch response, respectively, while dupilumab demonstrated consistent efficacy across all outcomes, supporting the role of targeted biologic therapy in PN. Because comparative estimates are derived from indirect evidence, head-to-head trials are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Subjective alcohol response across drinking contexts: a systematic review with bayesian meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Alcohol subjective response (SR) predicts drinking behaviour and risk for alcohol use disorder, but there is limited consensus on how SR differs across contexts, research settings, and alcohol problem severity. OBJECTIVES: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined how alcohol SR differs across (1) commercial (e.g., bar/club/restaurant) versus non-commercial (e.g., home) settings and (2) social versus solitary drinking contexts, and if these effects are moderated by (3) laboratory versus naturalistic study setting and (4) non-problem versus problem alcohol use. METHODS: Studies assessing alcohol SR across drinking contexts were systematically identified and synthesized. Outcomes included four SR quadrants (HIGH+, HIGH-, LOW+, LOW-) and alcohol reward (hedonic, motivational) and were analysed using random-effects Bayesian meta-analytic models. RESULTS: Across k = 15 studies, social and commercial contexts (versus solitary, non-commercial) were associated with enhanced HIGH + and alcohol reward (hedonic, motivational) effects, with potential LOW- attenuated effects. HIGH+ effects were stronger when drinking socially (versus alone) across research settings, with naturalistic environments possibly enhancing this effect. LOW- effects were potentially attenuated during social drinking only in naturalistic settings. Participants with problem alcohol use (versus non-problem) showed possible attenuation of LOW- effects while drinking socially (versus alone). Several planned analyses were limited by insufficient data. CONCLUSIONS: Alcohol SR varies by context and may be underestimated in laboratory settings. Limited studies, including heterogeneous effects (e.g., LOW+), were identified, underscoring the need to refine laboratory context manipulations, integrate ecologically valid approaches, and address gaps in how contextual features, SR domains, and problem severity shape alcohol SR.

articles.title: Obstetric pharmacotranscriptomics.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Pregnancy produces gestational-age and tissue-specific transcriptional remodeling in maternal blood, placenta, decidua, fetal membranes, and fetal compartments that can modify pathways governing drug disposition and response. Obstetric pharmacotranscriptomics seeks to relate these dynamic expression states to medication exposure, target engagement, efficacy, and toxicity. AREAS COVERED: This narrative review defines obstetric pharmacotranscriptomics, distinguishes pregnancy- and disease-associated expression from medication-induced transcriptional effects, and evaluates current evidence from maternal blood, cell-free RNA, placenta, and pregnancy-relevant experimental models. PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar were searched from database inception through 15 September 2026, using combinations of pregnancy, placenta, transcriptomics, RNA sequencing, pharmacotranscriptomics, drug response, medication exposure, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, cytochrome P450, UDP-glucuronosyltransferase (uridine 5'-diphospho-glucuronosyltransferase), ATP-binding cassettes, solute carrier transporters, and specific obstetric medications. Priority was given to human pregnancy studies, longitudinal designs, direct drug-perturbation experiments, and mechanistically informative preclinical studies. EXPERT OPINION: Pregnancy transcriptomics is substantially more mature than pregnancy pharmacotranscriptomics. The strongest path forward is to embed longitudinal transcriptomic sampling within pharmacokinetic and therapeutic studies so that gestational biology, drug exposure, target engagement, efficacy, and toxicity can be distinguished. Clinically useful signatures will require independent validation, tissue and cell-type specificity, demonstrated incremental value over standard clinical predictors, and conversion to reproducible targeted assays.

articles.title: Cucurbitacins as multitarget pharmacological modulators: chemistry, biosynthesis, molecular targets, regulated cell death, and translational challenges, with emphasis on cucurbitacin B and I.
articles.abstract: Cucurbitacins are highly oxidized tetracyclic triterpenoids with context-dependent pharmacological effects. This review focuses primarily on cucurbitacin B (CuB) and cucurbitacin I (CuI)-the most extensively characterized family members-while surveying the wider structural diversity of the cucurbitacin family. We integrate their chemistry, biosynthesis, and structure-activity relationships with structural interpretations of molecular target engagement and translational feasibility. We highlight how the electrophilic α,β-unsaturated ketone, C-17 side chain, acetylation, and glycosylation may influence potency and selectivity. Mechanistically, we evaluate Janus kinase 2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 signaling, ferroptosis involving solute carrier family 7 member 11 and glutathione peroxidase 4, PTEN-induced kinase 1-Parkin-dependent mitophagy, allosteric modulation of insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding protein 1, and NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3 inflammasome inhibition. We consider anti-inflammatory and hepatoprotective effects, tumor-associated macrophage repolarization, and sensitization to immune checkpoint blockade. Experimentally determined protein structures inform proposed covalent and allosteric interactions, but these models require direct target validation and biomarkers. We distinguish compound-specific findings from family-wide interpretations. Effects may vary with compound, dose, and disease context. By connecting these pathways to wax gourd genomic resources and synthetic-biology approaches, we consider opportunities for sustainable cucurbitacin production. However, low aqueous solubility, rapid clearance, hepatotoxicity, and a narrow therapeutic index constrain clinical translation. We assess nanoparticle formulations, solid dispersions, and structure-guided analog development as possible solutions. Distinct from cucurbitacin B-centered reviews, this synthesis integrates structural pharmacology, regulated cell death, immunomodulation, and biosynthetic engineering within a research roadmap prioritizing target validation, biomarkers, and preclinical assessment.

articles.title: Emerging therapeutic potential of Tamoxifen in psoriasis: a review of novel drug delivery approaches, patents and future scope.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Psoriasis is a chronic, non-communicable, hyper-proliferative epidermal-inflammation characterized by abnormal generation of inflammatory mediators and complex interactions between keratinocytes and immune cells. AREA COVERED: A comprehensive literature survey was performed using Elsevier, Espacenet, Google Scholar, and PubMed to select the relevant studies published. Articles were selected on the basis of relevant peer-reviewed publications focusing on topical drug delivery systems for Tamoxifen citrate (TMC) in Psoriasis. TMC is a selective estrogen receptor modulator showing emerging potential for psoriasis management because of its immunomodulatory and antiproliferative effects. This review highlights the problems associated with conventional TMC delivery like stability, high-dose requirement and adverse effects. It additionally emphasizes the evidences from research articles, case studies and patents. In addition, the review described in detail novel drug delivery methods and various strategies aimed at overcoming the key challenges associated with TMC and psoriasis. EXPERT OPINION: Conventional delivery systems show limited success in effectively treating psoriasis. The adherence of patients to these therapies is often low, attributed to various factors such as associated adverse effects & high costs. Therefore, it is essential to explore methods for providing effective treatment approaches. To address the need, innovative strategies are being investigated and created to enhance action.

articles.title: A Patient-Centered Approach for Drug-Drug Interaction (DDI) Assessment: Integrating Nested Clinical DDI Studies to Verify Translatability of Healthy Volunteer DDI Data, Minimize Stand-Alone Trials, and Enrich Drug Labeling.
articles.abstract: The pharmaceutical industry often adopts a stepwise approach, assuming that drug-drug interaction (DDI) results obtained in healthy volunteers (HVs) are translatable to patients. This strategy typically begins with evaluating DDIs in HVs using probe drugs, followed by assessing interactions with potential concomitant medications, often supported by physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling. Findings from HV studies are subsequently extrapolated to patient populations to inform drug labeling. However, this approach has limitations: (i) DDI results obtained from HV studies may not always be able be to translate to patients due to disease-related physiological changes; (ii) ethical and cost concerns arise when administering investigational drugs to HVs in clinical setting; and (iii) physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling may be insufficient in predicting DDIs across diverse clinical scenarios. One way to address these challenges is the nested DDI study, where DDI assessments are perceptively embedded within phase II or III clinical trials. [1]. We reviewed US Food and Drugs Administration approvals over recent decades and found that nested/patient-based DDI evaluations were considered sufficient by Food and Drug Administration to support DDI labeling for 86% of new chemical entities and 92% of biologics. This design helps verify HV-to-patient translatability, reduces HV exposure, lowers operational costs, and strengthens labeling. Importantly, nested DDI studies can confirm known interactions, uncover new DDIs, and address gaps in physiologically based pharmacokinetic predictions. In conclusion, prospectively integrating nested DDI studies into development programs supports efficient risk assessment, enhances patient safety, and improves clinical relevance. Regulators and drug developers should consider nested designs as a standard component of DDI evaluation.

articles.title: Evaluation of the Achievement of a Pharmacodynamic Target of Piperacillin-Tazobactam for the Population With Obesity: An Open Randomized Controlled Feasibility Study (TAZO-OBESITY Trial).
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Observational studies report that prolonged infusions of piperacillin-tazobactam may enable the achievement of an optimal clinically targeted free drug concentration above the minimum inhibitory concentration (fT > MIC). OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the feasibility of a randomized controlled trial (RCT) comparing standard to prolonged infusions of piperacillin-tazobactam in the obese population. METHODS: In this open-label RCT, patients with a body mass index (BMI) of 30 kg/m2 or higher who initiated piperacillin-tazobactam were recruited and randomly assigned to receive either standard or prolonged infusions of the antibiotic. Feasibility and safety outcomes were assessed. A blood sample was collected 24 h after the intervention to measure total piperacillin concentrations, with an exploratory aim of determining the proportion of patients who achieved 100% fT > MIC. RESULTS: A total of 45 patients were recruited at a rate of 7.2 patients per month with a consent rate of 42.1%, achieving these feasibility objectives. Adherence to blood sampling was 77.8%, below the 80% objective. On an exploratory basis, the proportion of patients who achieved 100% fT > MIC 24 h postintervention was 64.3% in the prolonged-infusion group and 55.6% in the standard-infusion group (p = 0.725). There was no significant difference in the safety outcomes (p = 0.756). CONCLUSION: This first RCT evaluating prolonged infusions of piperacillin-tazobactam in the obese population demonstrated the feasibility of the protocol. Although not statistically significant, the results suggest a favorable trend for fT > MIC attainment and no safety signal for prolonged infusions and support the conduct of a larger scale RCT. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical trial registration: NCT #06690905.

articles.title: 15-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (15-HETE)-GPR39 axis: a potential therapeutic target in eosinophilic asthma.
articles.abstract: Arachidonic acid (AA) metabolites play key roles in the pathophysiology of asthma. Along with cyclooxygenase and CYP P450, lipoxygenases (LO) produce these metabolites. 15-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (15-HETE), a product of 15-LO, has been implicated in severe asthma, particularly eosinophilic asthma. This article reviews the AA-15-HETE axis in eosinophilic asthma. 15-HETE contributes to key features of eosinophilic asthma, including eosinophil recruitment, mucus hypersecretion, and airway remodeling. Despite these observations, the downstream signaling mechanisms through which 15-HETE exerts its effects remain incompletely understood. GPR39 has recently been proposed as a potential receptor for 15-HETE, linking lipid metabolism to intracellular signaling involved in inflammation and tissue remodeling. Although the role of GPR39 in asthma has not been studied, its ability to respond to bioactive lipids suggests it may serve as a critical signaling node in eosinophilic inflammation. Taken together, these findings support a model in which the AA-15-HETE-GPR39 axis contributes to the pathogenesis of eosinophilic asthma. Targeting GPR39 may therefore represent a novel and underexplored therapeutic strategy for modulating airway inflammation and remodeling.

articles.title: Rotigotine transdermal patch in Parkinson's disease: a narrative review of pharmacology, clinical evidence, special-population management, and health economics.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Parkinson's disease (PD) requires lifelong dopaminergic therapy, yet oral routes are frequently compromised by gastrointestinal dysfunction, dysphagia, and perioperative fasting. Abrupt withdrawal of oral dopaminergic drugs may precipitate severe motor deterioration or parkinsonism-hyperpyrexia syndrome. Rotigotine transdermal patch delivers 24-h continuous dopaminergic stimulation (CDS) via a non-ergot dopamine agonist (DA) formulation that bypasses first-pass metabolism and gastrointestinal absorption, and may be particularly useful when oral dopaminergic delivery becomes unreliable or is not possible. OBJECTIVE: To synthesize published evidence on rotigotine pharmacology, clinical efficacy, management in vulnerable populations, safety, real-world effectiveness, and health economics, with emphasis on the incremental contribution of a scenario-based, Asia/China-inclusive, and pharmacy-oriented narrative relative to prior general reviews. METHODS: Narrative review of randomized controlled trials, meta-analyses, regulatory documents, pharmacoeconomic models, and prospective observational studies identified through structured literature search and bibliographic screening. RESULTS: Transdermal bioavailability is approximately 37% versus less than 5% for oral rotigotine. Pivotal Chinese trials SP0914 (early PD: UPDRS II + III -4.9 vs. -0.2) and SP1037 (advanced PD: placebo-adjusted off-time reduction -1.20 h/d [95% CI -1.83 to -0.57]; within-group change -2.36 h/d) demonstrated efficacy; meta-analyses support motor and selected non-motor benefits, including sleep, mood, and gastrointestinal tolerability, whereas swallowing-related signals remain preliminary and based mainly on small observational studies. Perioperative fasting, dysphagia, end-stage disease, and hepatorenal impairment represent clinically important scenarios in which non-oral delivery may be considered, although supporting evidence outside pivotal motor trials is often limited. Application-site reactions (ASRs) are the principal local adverse events; structured 14-day site rotation reduced ASR from 50.0% to 20.3% (P = 0.0373). Chinese cost-effectiveness analyses reported an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of 1,118,617.81 CNY per quality-adjusted life year versus pramipexole immediate-release at market price, with price-sensitivity thresholds of 28.5% and 9.5% reductions. CONCLUSION: Rotigotine provides CDS for patients with PD when oral delivery is unreliable; individualized patient selection, structured pharmaceutical care, and updated pharmacoeconomic evaluation are warranted.

articles.title: Anticoagulants beyond coagulation: repurposing heparin to mitigate immunothrombosis and inflammatory cascades in sepsis.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome caused by a dysregulated host response to infection, in which inflammation, coagulation, endothelial injury, and immune dysfunction interact to drive organ failure and death. Accumulating evidence identifies immunothrombosis as a central mechanism in this process, linking neutrophil extracellular traps, platelet activation, tissue factor expression, circulating histones, and glycocalyx degradation to microvascular collapse and multiple organ dysfunction. Although heparin has traditionally been used as an anticoagulant, its highly sulfated structure also permits interactions that are independent of antithrombin. In addition to inhibiting thrombin generation, heparin can neutralize extracellular histones, interfere with HMGB1- and lipopolysaccharide-related inflammatory signaling, inhibit heparanase, preserve endothelial glycocalyx integrity, and modulate leukocyte trafficking through selectin-related pathways. Most of these non-anticoagulant actions have been demonstrated in cell systems, animal models, human endotoxemia, or diseases other than sepsis, and should therefore be read as biological plausibility rather than as an established clinical effect. The clinical literature addresses three questions that should not be conflated: routine venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in critically ill patients, anticoagulation directed at sepsis-induced coagulopathy or disseminated intravascular coagulation, and experimental immunomodulatory repurposing. The most recent meta-analysis restricted to randomized trials found no significant mortality reduction with heparin across three trials and 426 patients (risk ratio 0.86, 95% confidence interval 0.60-1.24), and the disseminated intravascular coagulation subgroup was also inconclusive. Favorable associations reported in retrospective sepsis-induced coagulopathy cohorts justify prospective phenotype-enriched trials but do not identify established responders. This review summarizes the pathophysiological rationale, mechanistic basis, current clinical evidence, and major safety considerations of heparin use in sepsis, and highlights future directions including precision phenotyping, biomarker-guided therapy, and non-anticoagulant heparin derivatives. At present no heparin preparation, salt, dose, or biomarker threshold is validated for sepsis-specific immunomodulation.

articles.title: B7-H3 molecular imaging for the era of pan-cancer targeted therapy.
articles.abstract: B7-H3 (CD276) is broadly overexpressed across solid tumors and plays active roles in immune evasion, tumor angiogenesis, and metabolic reprogramming. As B7-H3-directed antibody-drug conjugates chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies, and radioimmunotherapy agents advance through clinical trials, non-invasive whole-body imaging of B7-H3 expression has become a pressing clinical need. Tissue biopsy with IHC cannot capture systemic target heterogeneity, and the recent IDeate-PanTumor01 trial found no correlation between baseline B7-H3 H-score and response to ifinatamab deruxtecan-illustrating the gap that molecular imaging must fill. This mini review surveys B7-H3-targeted imaging agents by scaffold class-antibodies, affibodies, nanobodies, and bicyclic peptides-and examines radioimmunotherapy platforms that couple PET-based dosimetry with targeted radionuclide delivery.

articles.title: Astragaloside IV attenuates ferroptosis-related testicular injury in rats with experimental varicocele.
articles.abstract: Varicocele is an important correctable cause of male infertility. Oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation contribute to the associated testicular injury, but the role of ferroptosis remains controversial. Astragaloside IV (AS-IV), a quality-control metabolite of Astragali radix, has antioxidant activity and can modulate ferroptosis-related processes, yet its effect in varicocele is unclear. This study evaluated whether AS-IV attenuates testicular injury in experimental varicocele and examined ferroptosis-related mechanisms. A Sprague-Dawley rat model was established by partial ligation of the left renal vein and treated with oral AS-IV; Ferrostatin-1 served as a pharmacological comparator. Label-free proteomics, histopathology, biochemical assays and targeted molecular analyses were combined with a TM4 Sertoli-cell model of RSL3-induced injury. AS-IV lessened tubular injury and improved Johnsen scores in a dose-related manner, reduced testicular Fe2+, ROS and MDA, and raised the GSH/GSSG ratio. Proteomics showed partial reversal of lipid-metabolism and ferroptosis-related enrichment after AS-IV. These changes were accompanied by recovery of androgen receptor (AR) and MBOAT2. In TM4 cells, AS-IV improved viability and lowered C11-BODIPY oxidation after RSL3; enzalutamide weakened the effects of AS-IV on lipid peroxidation and MBOAT2 and only partly reduced the viability rescue. The findings provide experimental evidence that AS-IV ameliorates varicocele-related testicular injury and that AR/MBOAT2-related signalling may participate.

articles.title: Anti-Nectin4 monoclonal antibodies attenuate airway inflammation and epithelial barrier dysfunction in asthma.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Nectin4 is an epithelial cell-adhesion molecule that may be involved in airway inflammatory responses. However, the effects of Nectin4 targeting in asthma has not yet been investigated. METHODS: Here we engineered anti-Nectin4 monoclonal antibody, N-1T1C8Ab or N-1T3H9Ab, their effects on airway epithelial dysfunction and inflammation. Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus 1 (Der p 1)-stimulated normal human bronchial epithelial (NHBE) cells and ovalbumin-induced asthmatic BALB/c mice were used as experimental models. RESULTS: Anti-Nectin4 antibody treatment restored epithelial barrier dysfunction and was associated with changes in IL-33-related, MyD88/IRAK, and Afadin/Rac1 signaling in NHBE cells. In the murine asthma model, administration of N-1T1C8Ab or N-1T3H9Ab reduced airway inflammation, airway resistance, and immune cell infiltration in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Histological analysis demonstrated decreased inflammatory cell infiltration, goblet cell hyperplasia, and fibrosis in lung tissues. Anti-Nectin4 antibody treatment was also associated with modulation of IL-33/MyD88-related signaling components. CONCLUSION: These findings indicate that anti-Nectin4 monoclonal antibodies attenuate airway inflammation and improve epithelial barrier function. Further preclinical studies are warranted to determine the potential of Nectin4 targeting in asthma.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of aficamten for obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: a model-based analysis from the perspective of the Chinese healthcare system.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of aficamten plus standard of care (SoC) versus SoC alone for patients with symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM) from the perspective of the Chinese healthcare system. METHODS: A four-state Markov model based on the phase III SEQUOIA-HCM trial was developed to simulate lifetime outcomes. The first 24 weeks were modeled using trial data, followed by 4-week cycles for long-term extrapolation. Based on FOREST-HCM, the incremental treatment effect of aficamten was assumed to persist through week 96 and then linearly wane to complete loss by year 3. Costs and health outcomes were discounted at 4.5% annually. Model uncertainty was assessed using one-way sensitivity analysis, probabilistic sensitivity analysis, and scenario analyses. RESULTS: Total costs were US$143,281.22 with aficamten plus SoC and US$96,509.03 with SoC alone, with 9.696 and 7.643 QALYs, respectively. Aficamten plus SoC yielded an incremental cost of US$46,772.19 and 2.054 QALYs, corresponding to an ICER of US$22,775.17/QALY, below the WTP threshold of US$29,399.70/QALY. The probability of being cost-effective was 76.6% at the WTP threshold. Scenario analyses showed ICERs of US$19,351.77/QALY when only short-term effects were considered, US$43,752.42/QALY when treatment effects disappeared in year 5, and US$81,220.72/QALY when they disappeared in year 10. Price reductions of 22.0% and 50.5%, respectively, were required in the latter two scenarios. With a permanent discontinuation probability of 0.131% per 4-week cycle, the ICER was US$23,888.94/QALY. CONCLUSION: From the Chinese healthcare system perspective, aficamten plus SoC was cost-effective versus SoC alone for symptomatic oHCM under the base-case assumptions.

articles.title: Comparative real-world pharmacovigilance analysis of adverse event signals associated with six approved CAR-T products using the FAERS database.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Although several CAR-T products have been approved for hematologic malignancies, their post-marketing adverse-event reporting patterns may not be interchangeable. This study compared FAERS-derived positive signals across approved CAR-T products to distinguish recurrent class-related toxicities from product-skewed reporting patterns. METHODS: FAERS reports from Q1 2014 to Q2 2025 were reviewed for CAR-T products. Demographic characteristics were summarized for seven products, whereas PT- and SOC-level signal analyses were restricted to six products with sufficient signal data: Breyanzi, Kymriah, Tecartus, Yescarta, Abecma, and Carvykti. Positive signals were detected using ROR, PRR, and BCPNN algorithms. After predefined exclusion of nonclinical or non-AE terms, indication- or disease-progression-related terms, procedure- or investigation-related terms, efficacy- or persistence-related terms, and product-quality-related terms, eligible signals were compared at the PT and SOC levels. Nonspecific MedDRA-coded PTs were retained if they met the predefined signal criteria, but they were interpreted descriptively and were not used to define product-level profile labels. RESULTS: CRS was consistently among the leading PT-level signals across all six products. Yescarta and Tecartus showed higher reporting of ICANS and neurotoxicity-related PTs. Kymriah was more strongly represented by infection-, immune-, and hematologic-related signals, whereas Carvykti showed several neurologic PTs including Parkinsonism, cranial nerve paralysis, facial paralysis, and Bell's palsy. Abecma showed relatively high-ranking systemic symptom-related PTs, including fatigue, headache, and decreased appetite. At the SOC level, nervous system disorders and infections and infestations were among the most frequently represented categories, but their proportions differed across products. CONCLUSION: FAERS-based signal detection showed a common CAR-T reporting backbone centered on CRS, ICANS/neurotoxicity, hypotension, pyrexia, infection-related events, and hematologic events, together with product-skewed signal patterns. These findings represent disproportionality signals rather than comparative safety rankings, and FAERS data cannot establish causal relationships between CAR-T products and adverse events.

articles.title: 5-HT2A receptor activation induces CB1-dependent presynaptic inhibitory long-term depression in the nucleus accumbens core.
articles.abstract: The serotonin 2A receptor (5-HT2A) is a Gq/11-coupled receptor implicated in reward processing, neuropsychiatric disorders, and the actions of serotonergic psychedelics. Although 5-HT2A activation has been shown to engage endocannabinoid (eCB) signaling in several brain regions, its role in inhibitory synaptic plasticity within the nucleus accumbens (NAc) remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether 5-HT2A activation modulates GABAergic synaptic transmission onto medium spiny neurons (MSNs) in the mouse NAc core. Using whole-cell patch-clamp recordings, we found that activation of 5-HT2A receptors with the selective agonist TCB-2 induced a robust inhibitory long-term depression (iLTD) of evoked GABAergic synaptic transmission. This depression was accompanied by reduced spontaneous and miniature IPSC frequency, increased paired-pulse ratio, and changes in coefficient of variation analysis consistent with a presynaptic reduction in GABA release probability. Mechanistically, iLTD was occluded by the CB1 receptor agonist WIN55,212-2 and blocked by the CB1 receptor antagonist AM251, supporting a critical role for endocannabinoid signaling. Furthermore, iLTD induction required postsynaptic G-protein signaling, phospholipase Cβ (PLCβ) activity, and synthesis of the endocannabinoid 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG). Together, these findings demonstrate that 5-HT2A activation induces a CB1-dependent presynaptic iLTD through a postsynaptic PLCβ/2-AG signaling cascade. These results demonstrate that 5-HT2A receptor activation engages endocannabinoid signaling to regulate inhibitory synaptic transmission in the NAc, highlighting a mechanism through which 5-HT2A signaling may modulate mesolimbic circuit function.

articles.title: The pharmacokinetics and pharmacogenomics of voriconazole in pediatric Saudi patients: advancing toward precision medicine.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Voriconazole is a broad-spectrum triazole antifungal. It is used to prevent and treat invasive fungal infections in immunocompromised pediatric patients. Its clinical use is limited due to its nonlinear pharmacokinetics, high variability, and a narrow therapeutic index. Data on pharmacogenomic effects in pediatric patients are limited, particularly in the Saudi population. This study aimed to evaluate voriconazole pharmacokinetics in pediatric patients and to assess the impact of CYP2C19 genotypes on drug concentrations and clearance. METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted from October 2022 to October 2024 at two tertiary care centers in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Saudi pediatric patients aged between 1 and 14 years receiving voriconazole were enrolled after informed consent from guardians. Trough blood samples were collected on the fifth day of therapy and CYP2C19 genotyping (*2, *3, *17) was performed. The metabolizer status was assigned according to the Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guidelines. RESULTS: Forty patients were included. The mean age was 67.7 ± 44.1 months, and the mean weight was 17.8 ± 9.5 kg CYP2C19 phenotypes were distributed as follows: normal metabolizers (65%), rapid metabolizers (17.5%), intermediate metabolizers (10%), and ultrarapid metabolizers (7.5%). No poor metabolizers were observed. The mean voriconazole trough concentration was 2.26 ± 2.68 mg/L and the majority (52.5%) of patients had subtherapeutic levels, 35% were within range, and 12.5% were supratherapeutic. In the multivariable analysis, only weight was significantly associated with clearance (R 2 = 0.14, P-value = 0.02), whereas genotype showed no significant effect (P-value = 0.48). CONCLUSION: Voriconazole trough concentrations showed considerable variability among pediatric patients. Thirty-five percent of patients achieved therapeutic trough concentrations at the first trough assessment and no statistically significant association between CYP2C19 polymorphisms and voriconazole trough concentrations was observed in this cohort. However, the small sample size may have limited the detection of genetic influences. These findings support the conclusion that individualized dosing is needed to optimize therapy.

articles.title: Risk prediction model for pegaspargase-associated severe coagulopathy and blood product costs: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Pegaspargase-induced severe coagulopathy (SC) is a common complication in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) treatment, yet reliable predictive tools are limited and its economic burden remains unclear. This study developed and internally validated a clinical prediction nomogram for SC, concurrently created a web-based calculator, and quantified the impact of coagulopathy on the cost of blood products. METHODS: Using retrospective data from 356 pediatric patients treated according to the Chinese Children's Leukemia Group Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia 2018 protocol at Hebei Children's Hospital between January 2020 and August 2025, SC was defined as grade 4 fibrinogen reduction or grade ≥3 prolongation of the activated partial thromboplastin time. A nomogram was developed via multivariate logistic regression, and cost drivers were analyzed by multiple linear regression. RESULTS: Hypoalbuminemia, elevated bilirubin, and elevated procalcitonin were independent predictors of SC. The nomogram achieved an area under the curve of 0.819 (95% CI: 0.773-0.864), and decision curve analysis indicated favorable clinical utility. Blood product cost was primarily driven by patient age, product type, and transfusion frequency (adjusted R 2 = 0.677). DISCUSSION: This study developed an accurate predictive model for SC and clarified the associated economic burden, providing evidence to support clinical vigilance and inform healthcare resource planning.

articles.title: Neuroprotective effects of hydroxytyrosol against monosodium glutamate-induced hippocampal and cerebellar injury in rats.
articles.abstract: Monosodium glutamate (MSG) is a widely used food additive associated with neurotoxicity through excitotoxicity, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and apoptosis. The present study investigated the neuroprotective effects of hydroxytyrosol (HT), a naturally occurring phenolic compound with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, against MSG-induced brain and cerebellar injury in rats. Thirty-two male Wistar albino rats were randomly assigned to four groups (Control, MSG, HT, and MSG + HT). MSG (2 g/kg) and HT (10 mg/kg) were administered intraperitoneally for 21 days. Oxidative stress markers, inflammatory cytokines, myelin basic protein (MBP), histopathological alterations, and immunohistochemical markers of glial activation and apoptosis were evaluated. MSG administration significantly increased malondialdehyde (MDA), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) levels while decreasing glutathione (GSH), superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), and MBP levels in both brain and cerebellar tissues. Histopathological examination revealed marked neuronal degeneration, whereas immunohistochemical analyses demonstrated increased GFAP, S100β, and Bax expression together with reduced Bcl-2 immunoreactivity. HT treatment markedly attenuated these biochemical, histopathological, and immunohistochemical alterations by restoring antioxidant defenses, suppressing inflammatory responses, preserving MBP expression, reducing glial activation, and improving the Bax/Bcl-2 balance. These findings demonstrate that HT exerts neuroprotective effects against MSG-induced brain and cerebellar injury through coordinated antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, myelin-preserving, and anti-apoptotic mechanisms. The integrated evaluation of biochemical, histopathological, and immunohistochemical alterations highlights HT's potential as a promising candidate for preventing oxidative and inflammatory neurotoxicity.

articles.title: Stress-induced reinstatement of nicotine conditioned place preference in a rodent model of dopamine dysregulation: genetic, behavioral and molecular correlates of drug abuse vulnerability.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Schizophrenia and related psychoses are accompanied by poor stress adaptation and a high prevalence of cigarette smoking, contributing to reduced treatment adherence and poor quality of life. The mechanistic contributions to stress-induced drug-seeking in psychosis remain poorly understood. OBJECTIVES: The present study evaluated nicotine conditioned place preference (CPP) stress reinstatement in a heritable rodent model of dopamine dysregulation relevant to psychosis, alongside molecular and epigenetic alterations associated with drug use vulnerability. METHODS: Adolescent offspring (F1) of Sprague-Dawley rats treated neonatally with saline (MSxFS) or quinpirole (MQxFQ) were assessed for nicotine CPP expression, extinction, and restraint stress-induced reinstatement. One hour following stress, nucleus accumbens (NAc) and amygdala tissue were analyzed for CREB and dynorphin expression, with complementary single-nucleus RNA sequencing used to identify cell-type-specific genetic adaptations in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) of adolescent rats. RESULTS: MQxFQ rats exhibited enhanced nicotine CPP, resistance to extinction, and robust stress-induced reinstatement relative to MSxFS controls. Following nicotine and stress exposure, MQxFQ rats showed reduced CREB in the NAc and increased CREB and dynorphin in the amygdala. Differential gene expression profiling in the mPFC revealed cell-type specific metabolic and plasticity-related neuroadaptations consistent with cortical vulnerability to psychosis and drug use. CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate significant expression of stress-induced reinstatement in a heritable model of dopamine dysregulation. Convergent molecular and genetic adaptations implicate dysregulated stress and reward circuitry, providing a mechanistic framework linking genetic risk for psychosis to maladaptive drug-seeking and vulnerability to stress.

articles.title: TRPV1 mediates tetrathiomolybdate-induced muscle hypertrophy via peroxynitrite-dependent redox signaling.
articles.abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS), notably superoxide (O2•-), serve as essential signaling molecules for muscle remodeling. While tetrathiomolybdate (TM)-O2•- axis can induce myofiber hypertrophy, the precise redox signaling mechanisms remain incompletely understood. In this study, transient receptor potential cation channel subfamily V member 1 (TRPV1) is identified as a critical mediator of TM-O2•--induced hypertrophy through transcriptome analysis and functional validation. Genetic and pharmacological manipulation demonstrates TRPV1's essential role downstream of O2•-, where TRPV1 knockout abolishes while its activation mimics TM-induced hypertrophy effects. O2•- stimulates nitric oxide synthase (NOS) activity and nitric oxide (NO) production, leading to formation of peroxynitrite (ONOO-) which directly activates TRPV1. The ONOO--TRPV1 axis is specifically required for hypertrophy, as ONOO- scavengers block TRPV1 activation and hypertrophy despite normal O2•- and NO levels. In conclusion, these findings reveal TRPV1 as a redox-sensitive mediator that orchestrates superoxide-triggered muscle remodeling via the ONOO--TRPV1 axis.

articles.title: Danmu Jingao Tablet attenuates periodontitis by promoting SIRT3-mediated SOD2 deacetylation and mitochondrial redox homeostasis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Nauclea officinalis (Pierre ex Pit.) Merr. & Chun is a traditional medicinal plant widely used by the Li ethnic group in Hainan Province, China. Danmu Jingao Tablet (DMJGT), a Chinese patent medicine derived from this plant, exhibits well-documented anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease characterized by progressive alveolar bone resorption, in which macrophage oxidative stress and M1 polarization are key drivers. However, whether DMJGT exerts its anti-periodontitis effects through regulating macrophage polarization remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate whether DMJGT ameliorates periodontitis by upregulating SIRT3 expression and enhancing the SIRT3-mediated SOD2 deacetylation pathway, thereby suppressing macrophage oxidative stress, preserving mitochondrial function, and modulating macrophage polarization. MATERIALS AND METHODS: DMJGT constituents were analyzed by UPLC-Q-TOF-MS, with molecular docking, MD simulations, and SPR predicting compound-SIRT3 binding. In ligature-induced periodontitis mice, alveolar bone loss and histopathology were evaluated by Micro-CT and staining. In LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages, ROS, mitochondrial function, oxidative stress markers, protein levels (SIRT3, SOD2, Ac-SOD2, TFAM, PGC-1α, CD86, CD206), and mRNA (Sirt3, Il1b, Il6, Tnf) were assessed. SIRT3 dependency was confirmed by 3-TYP inhibition in vivo and siRNA knockdown in vitro. RESULTS: Eighty-three compounds were identified, with strictosamide, vincosamide, and naucleofficine A showing high binding affinity to SIRT3. DMJGT reduced alveolar bone loss, osteoclasts, and inflammation. It upregulated SIRT3, TFAM, and PGC-1α, decreased Ac-SOD2 (K68), restored redox markers, suppressed M1 and promoted M2 polarization, and reduced cytokines. 3-TYP or Sirt3 siRNA reversed these effects. CONCLUSIONS: DMJGT alleviates periodontitis by upregulating SIRT3 expression and enhancing the SIRT3-mediated SOD2 deacetylation pathway. This pathway reduces oxidative stress, preserves mitochondrial function, and reprograms macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype. SIRT3 is a critical target for DMJGT, providing a new mechanistic basis for its clinical application in periodontitis.

articles.title: Tao-He-Cheng-Qi decoction protects against sepsis-associated acute lung injury by modulating gut microbiota and succinate-associated pulmonary macrophage polarization.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Sepsis-associated acute lung injury (SA-ALI) has high mortality and limited therapies.Tao-He-Cheng-Qi decoction protects against sepsis-associated acute lung injury by modulating gut microbiota and succinate-associated pulmonary macrophage polarization. AIM OF THE STUDY: To evaluate the protective effects of THCQ pretreatment against LPS-induced SA-ALI and examine associated changes in gut microbiota, succinate levels, SUCNR1-PKA-CREB signaling and macrophage polarization. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A murine SA-ALI model was induced by intraperitoneal LPS. Lung injury, inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α), and M1/M2 polarization were assessed. Gut microbiota was analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing. Succinate levels, SUCNR1, and PKA-CREB signaling were measured. Microbiota dependence was tested using antibiotic depletion, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from THCQ-treated donors, exogenous succinate, and macrophage depletion with clodronate liposomes. RESULTS: THCQ pretreatment attenuated lung injury, reduced IL-1β and TNF-α levels, and shifted pulmonary macrophage polarization toward an M2-like phenotype. These effects were accompanied by altered gut microbiota composition, a lower abundance ratio of bacterial families grouped in the exploratory succinate-metabolism analysis, reduced serum and pulmonary succinate levels, lower SUCNR1 expression, and increased PKA/CREB phosphorylation. Antibiotic treatment attenuated the protective responses to THCQ, while FMT from THCQ-treated donors reproduced improvements in lung injury. Exogenous succinate attenuated THCQ-mediated protection. Clo-Lipo treatment reduced the proportions of alveolar and interstitial macrophages and markedly attenuated the protective effects of THCQ. CONCLUSION: THCQ treatment protects against SA-ALI and suppresses M1-like macrophage polarization. These effects are accompanied by changes in gut microbiota composition, reduced succinate levels, and altered SUCNR1-PKA-CREB signaling. Together, the findings support a role for gut microbiota-metabolism-immune interactions in the protective effects of THCQ.

articles.title: 10-Gingerol attenuates alcohol-induced colon injury by modulating IL-36R and downstream cGAS-STING signaling to suppress macrophage inflammation and ferroptosis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Ginger (Zingiber officinale Roscoe, Zingiberaceae) is traditionally used in Chinese and Ayurvedic/Tibb-Unani medicine for gastrointestinal and inflammatory disorders. Its bioactive constituent 10-gingerol (10-G) exhibits intestinal anti-inflammatory activity, providing a rationale for investigating its protective effects against alcohol-induced colon injury. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate whether 10-G attenuates alcohol-induced colon injury by modulating interleukin-36 receptor (IL-36R) and downstream cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling, thereby reducing macrophage inflammation and ferroptosis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An alcohol-induced mouse colon injury model and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated mouse peritoneal macrophages (MPMs) were used. Transcriptomics, Il1rl2 knockdown, complementary target-engagement assays, and STING-agonist rescue were performed. RESULTS: 10-G reduced IL-36R and cGAS expression and STING signaling activation, while attenuating alcohol-induced colon injury, tight-junction disruption, inflammation, and ferroptosis-related alterations. Target-engagement assays supported IL-36R engagement by 10-G. In vivo, Il1rl2 knockdown suppressed cGAS-STING signaling and attenuated inflammation- and ferroptosis-related alterations. In LPS-stimulated MPMs, 10-G attenuated inflammatory responses and ferroptosis. Il1rl2 knockdown induced changes consistent with 10-G treatment; significant shRNA × 10-G interactions indicated that the effects of 10-G were influenced by IL-36R functional status. STING reactivation counteracted the effects of 10-G and Il1rl2 knockdown on inflammatory and ferroptosis-related readouts without restoring IL-36R levels. CONCLUSIONS: 10-G attenuates alcohol-induced colon injury by engaging and modulating IL-36R and suppressing downstream cGAS-STING signaling, thereby reducing macrophage inflammation and ferroptosis. Genetic and pharmacological evidence supports a functional upstream role for IL-36R.

articles.title: Oxcarbazepine-loaded nanoemulsions in thermosensitive nasal gels for epilepsy: in-vitro and in-vivo evaluation in status epilepticus rat model.
articles.abstract: To overcome the low aqueous solubility of oxcarbazepine (OXC), a BCS Class II drug, and to enhance brain exposure following intranasal administration, OXC was formulated into a self-nanoemulsifying drug delivery system (SNEDDS) incorporated within a thermosensitive nasal gel. The optimized SNEDDS (SNE.O2), comprising rose oil, Tween 80, and Transcutol® P, exhibited a droplet size of 10.38 nm, a zeta potential of -15.3 mV, and 97.24% drug content. SNE.O2 was dispersed into a hydrogel containing 16% Poloxamer 407, 1% Poloxamer 188, and 1.5% sodium carboxymethyl cellulose, yielding the optimum nanogel NG3.6. The nanogel had a gelation temperature of 30.9 °C, and viscosities of 600 and 720 cP at 25 and 31 °C, respectively. Ex-vivo buffalo mucosal permeation from NG3.6 showed a 1.67-fold enhancement compared to OXC control gel. in-vivo pharmacokinetics demonstrated 7.7 and 13.0-fold improvements for NG3.6 over the oral suspension, and 1.6-fold and 1.9 improvements over C3, for Cmax and AUC0-last, respectively. Brain-to-plasma ratios were 2.55 for NG3.6 compared to 1.67 and 0.26 for C3 and the oral suspension, respectively, demonstrating enhanced brain delivery. In status epilepticus rat model, NG3.6 significantly suppressed NF-κB, IL-1β and reduced the median Racine score when compared to Li/Pil group. However, NG3.6 did not show significant score compared to C3. Moreover, no overt short term histological abnormalities were observed. Ultimately, NG3.6 provides a promising brain delivery system with the potential to improve oxcarbazepine delivery to CNS. Further studies are needed to establish its therapeutic advantage and whether it can reduce dosage requirements and systemic side effects.

articles.title: Poly(vinyl alcohol) dissolving microneedles for transdermal semaglutide delivery and anti-obesity therapy in rats.
articles.abstract: Semaglutide is an effective anti-obesity peptide, but repeated subcutaneous injections may reduce its acceptability for long-term therapy. We prepared semaglutide-loaded poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) dissolving microneedles (Sema-MNs) by sequential vacuum-assisted molding and room-temperature drying. The 15 × 15 arrays concentrated Cy5-labelled semaglutide toward the needle tips, resisted axial compression, penetrated rat skin, and partially dissolved within 5 min; skin barrier function approached baseline within 4-6 h. Sema-MNs contained 29 ± 2 μg semaglutide per patch, with an apparent delivered amount of 18 ± 2 μg (63 ± 3%; n = 3), and released more than 90% of the Sema-Cy5-associated cargo within 30 min. In high-fat-diet-induced obese rats, once-daily Sema-MN treatment for 7 days reduced food intake and body weight. Treatment also decreased adipocyte size and hepatic lipid accumulation, improved glucose tolerance and serum metabolic indices, and reduced hypothalamic neuropeptide Y immunofluorescence relative to the disease and unloaded-microneedle controls. No evident renal biochemical or major-organ histopathological abnormalities were observed during the study. These findings support the feasibility of a compositionally simple, rapid-release PVA microneedle system for transdermal semaglutide administration.

articles.title: Antibody-aptamer conjugate for shear-triggered tissue plasminogen activator release and thrombolysis.
articles.abstract: Pathological blood clots cause life-threatening events, including ischemic stroke and myocardial infarction. Tissue plasminogen activator (TPA), a clinically approved fibrinolytic agent, remains a frontline therapy for clot dissolution. However, its short plasma half-life and requirement for high systemic doses pose serious risks, particularly hemorrhagic complications. To address these limitations, a shear-responsive delivery platform was engineered for controlled TPA release under pathological high-shear conditions. This system, termed Single-MOlecule-based materials with structures and functions REsponsive to Shear (SMORES), consists of a shear-amplifying microparticle conjugated to a TPA-binding aptamer and functionalized with a monoclonal antibody against integrin αIIbβ3 as a platelet-targeting element.
